implementerProof.how: All three of the implementer's proofs were driven again from builds of my own, on a Postgres 17.11 + pgvector 0.8.0 of my own, not from its artifacts (the pod was replaced mid-round and every artifact of its rig went with the disk). A3 was re-driven as an independent main-against-head HTTP equivalence run on a fixture of my own with a main-against-main noise control; the panic criterion was re-run with its own negative control re-applied; the SuggestionKind reuse was measured again at the HTTP surface with CPU profiles of both builds rather than from the Go benchmark.

failures.criterion: A5, required checks and suites: the suites green at the head, main's known reds apart
failures.evidence: The `envoy-go-race` lane is red at the code head 612648e7 (https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/actions/runs/40852446247/job/123378703098) and the cause is this pull request's own new tests. That lane runs `go test -race -timeout 30m ./internal/dispatch/docs/ ...` (.github/workflows/envoy-and-contracts.yaml:1425). The docs package reports `FAIL github.com/sjawhar/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs 1801.513s` with `panic: test timed out after 30m0s`; it reports no data race at all (`WARNING: DATA RACE` appears 0 times in the whole job log), so the lane is red purely on elapsed time. On main the same package fits, but barely: 1745.847s at 8a911ecc (run 40857522211, lane green), 1738.382s at a7c762f6, 1731.084s at 5443d99b, 1705.994s at e21cfc61 — 54 to 94 seconds of headroom against the 1800 s cap. This branch's three new test files cost far more than that headroom: `go test -race -timeout 30m ./internal/dispatch/docs/ -run 'TestForkReads|TestAPanickedWriteLeavesNoForkForTheTransactionsLaterWrites|TestWriteCorpus' -count=1` takes 277.686s on its own in the issue pod (CGO_ENABLED=1, Postgres 17.11 + pgvector 0.8.0 on 127.0.0.1:55533), with TestWriteCorpus skipping for want of DISPATCH_TOKEN_CORPUS. The overflow also takes a second test down with it: `TestThreeBrowsersAndTheAPIEditOneRoomAtOnce` fails at the head with `room_peers_race_test.go:43: the test binary's deadline leaves 1m29.774s, not more than overlapMargin (1m30s): raise -timeout or lower overlapMargin for a local run` — that test refuses to run when the remaining deadline is under its own margin, so every branch that lands this overflow loses it too. `envoy-go-race` is not among main's required checks (`lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, `pr-title`, from `gh api repos/sjawhar/legion/rules/branches/main`), all four of which are green at 612648e7, so GitHub would still merge the head; the lane is red all the same, and it was green on main before this branch. No red test of mine pins this: the artefact that catches it is the lane itself, and a Go test asserting that a package finishes inside its own CI timeout would be a check of a check, which this deployment's instructions rule out. The fix is the implementer's to choose — the obvious ones are cutting the new tests' cost (the warm/cold matrices in fork_reads_test.go and panicked_fork_test.go each build real-size documents) or raising that step's `-timeout`, which is a shared-CI change and needs the architect.

All 21 markdown snapshots are byte-identical across main, head and a second main run (sha256 of each `text.markdown`, compared in order). The seeded document's token is the same string on every one of the five server runs of the round, `sha256:bd58ca7c06a33a7e8e06fa900f155ef8999e787cc476ed9691b85c07e6f369c6`. The only differing fields are 15 `blocks[].token`, 7 `text.token` and 1 `doc-edit.token`, which the normaliser cannot settle because a token hashes over content carrying freshly minted mark UUIDs; `diff cmp-main-head.txt cmp-main-main.txt` is empty, so the main-against-head difference is exactly the main-against-main difference, record for record and count for count.

After the three refusals the document reads 200,572 bytes at the same token, so a refused write leaves no trace of its fork or rendering.

proof.criterion: A panicked write leaves no fork or rendering for its transaction's later writes (C3, the architect's criterion 1)
proof.surface: docs package against Postgres 17.11 + pgvector 0.8.0, real-size generated document, warm and cold rooms — the panic is a ygo type observer failing in phase 2, which no HTTP route can provoke
proof.observed: PASS at the head, warm and cold.
proof.negativeControl: With `liveOperation.abandon` put back to main's condition (`op.recorded || len(op.updates) == 0`) the test FAILS in both rooms: `after the panic the write holds a fork = true and a rendering = true, want neither`; `docTree after the panic: fork reads {read:0 renderingReused:1}, want {read:1 renderingReused:0}`; `the fork after the further write holds the panicked text`; and the consequence a reader would meet, `version 3 records 410328 bytes of markdown, not the committed document's 410317 bytes`. The edit was reverted with `jj restore` straight after.

proof.criterion: A reuse never serves a rendering of a fork the room has moved under it
proof.surface: docs package against the same Postgres: anchored comment, suggestion, edit-and-version, accept, and a browser commit landing between two operations of one transaction, warm and cold
proof.negativeControl: With `buildFork`'s `write.dropRendering()` removed from its incremental branch (livewrite.go:594-596), so a fork the room moved keeps its rendering, `TestForkReadsEveryReuseOfAWritesRenderingDescribesItsFork/warm/a_browser_commit_between_operations` FAILS: `a write's rendering is not its fork's` at docTree, at capture and at publish, `SuggestionKind: fork reads {read:0 renderingReused:1}, want {read:1 renderingReused:0}`, and `version 5 records 410330 bytes of markdown, not the committed document's 410335 bytes`. Reverted with `jj restore` straight after.

notes: The aliasing contract the change introduces — `docTree` inside a write transaction now hands back the write's own tree, which 'a caller must never change' (livewrite.go:733-738) — was audited rather than assumed. The six consumers are VerifyMark, BlockForQuote, SuggestionKind, prevalidateLiveOperations, currentToken and an ApplyOps with no operation. Five read only (readAnchored, pmdoc.FindQuote, pmdoc.BlockIDForRange, pmdoc.MarkAttrs, nodeToken, checkEditPrecondition). The sixth, prevalidateLiveOperations, runs applyOperationsWithValidation over the tree; a throwaway in-package probe (since deleted) showed that path leaves its input's token unchanged, because applyOperation returns a new tree, and in any case the only route to it, ApplyOps with a precondition and a table-anchor operation, reaches docTree before the transaction has written anything, so the write holds no rendering to hand back. applyLive's own before-tree, which stampAskBlockIDs and applyOperations do mutate, is still a fresh readFork (mutation.go:258), not a reuse. Nothing enforces the contract for a consumer added later; the `checkRendering` hook catches a violation at the next reuse or at publish, but only in tests.

Environment: the issue pod was replaced in the middle of this round, which took the sibling Postgres harness, the INFRA-512 replay seed and the LINUX corpus with it. Every figure above comes from a rig I rebuilt afterwards — Debian postgresql-17 17.11-0+deb13u1 and postgresql-17-pgvector 0.8.0 unpacked onto the issue volume — and from a synthetic 200,572-byte spec seeded over the HTTP API, not from the implementer's corpus. TestWriteCorpus and TestWriteCorpusReadsOnce skip without DISPATCH_TOKEN_CORPUS, which this pod has no copy of.
